In a substitution language, each word has one distinct code. Code order is arbitrary.
rural digital secure = ka pa ni
rural access banking = mi su ni
digital access growth = ka vo su
secure banking growth = mi vo pa
rural digital growth = ka vo ni

questions.stem: In a queue of 42 candidates, a candidate is 21th from the front. After moving 4 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 18. New front rank = 21+4 = 25. Back rank = 42 − 25 + 1 = 18.

questions.stem: In a queue of 56 candidates, a candidate is 14th from the front. After moving 3 places towards the back, what is the candidate’s rank from the back?
questions.explanation: Answer: 40. New front rank = 14+3 = 17. Back rank = 56 − 17 + 1 = 40.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 112 km east, turns left and walks 216 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 234. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 90 km along the initial direction and 216 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(90² + 216²) = 234 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 38 km south, turns left and walks 30 km, then turns left and walks 22 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 34. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 16 km along the initial direction and 30 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(16² + 30²) = 34 km.

questions.stem: A surveyor walks 141 km west, turns left and walks 255 km, then turns left and walks 5 km. What is the shortest distance (km) from the starting point?
questions.explanation: Answer: 289. The first and third legs oppose each other. Net components are 136 km along the initial direction and 255 km perpendicular to it. Distance = √(136² + 255²) = 289 km.

questions.stem:

Conclusions:
I. All coins are tokens.
II. No cards is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Neither I nor II follows. A need not be contained in D. Some B are C and therefore D, contradicting II.

questions.stem:
Statements: No coins is a cards. Some cards are bonds. All bonds are tokens.
Conclusions:
I. All coins are tokens.
II. Some tokens are cards.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only II follows. The B–C overlap is inside D, proving II. No universal A–D relation is given.

questions.stem:
Statements: Some coins are cards. All cards are bonds. No bonds is a tokens.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are bonds.
II. Some cards are tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Only I follows. The stated A–B overlap lies in C. Since B is contained in C, no B can be D.

questions.stem:
Statements: Only a few coins are cards. All cards are bonds. No bonds is a tokens.
Conclusions:
I. Some coins are not cards.
II. No cards is a tokens.
questions.explanation: Answer: Both I and II follow. Only a few means some are and some are not. All B are C and no C is D excludes every B from D.

questions.stem: H is the brother of F. F is the mother of C. D is the father of H and F. How is H related to C?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal uncle. H is the brother of C’s mother F. Therefore H is the maternal uncle.

questions.stem: E is the mother of G. B is the daughter of G. H is the father of G. How is B related to H?
questions.explanation: Answer: Granddaughter. H is a parent of G, and B is G’s daughter. Hence B is H’s grandchild.

questions.stem: F is the only daughter of C. C is the father of F. G is the son of F. B is the sister of C. How is C related to G?
questions.explanation: Answer: Maternal grandfather. C is the father of F, and F is G’s mother. Thus C is the maternal grandfather.

questions.stem: A container holds 160 litres of pure milk. 32 litres are removed and replaced with water. This process is repeated once more, mixing thoroughly each time. How many litres of milk remain? (Round to two decimal places if needed.)

questions.stem: A 190 m train moving at 64.8 km/h overtakes a runner moving in the same direction at 14.4 km/h. Find the time (seconds, to two decimals) to pass the runner.
questions.explanation: Answer: 13.57. Relative speed = (64.8 − 14.4) ×5/18 = 14 m/s. Time = 190/14.

questions.stem: [Table set] The rejected category at D is what percentage of the approved category at B? (Round to two decimal places.)
questions.explanation: Answer: 67.11. Derived data: A: first category 960, second category 720; B: first category 1520, second category 1140; C: first category 800, second category 600; D: first category 680, second category 1020; E: first category 720, second category 960. 1020 ÷ 1520 × 100 = 67.11%.

questions.stem: [Table set] If 25% of the rejected category at E is transferred to the approved category there, what is the new size of the approved category at E?
questions.explanation: Answer: 960. Derived data: A: first category 960, second category 720; B: first category 1520, second category 1140; C: first category 800, second category 600; D: first category 680, second category 1020; E: first category 720, second category 960. New first category = 720 + 25% of 960.

questions.stem: [Table set] A new branch F has a total equal to the average total at A and E. Its categories are split in ratio 2:3. What is the number in its second category?
questions.explanation: Answer: 1008. Derived data: A: first category 960, second category 720; B: first category 1520, second category 1140; C: first category 800, second category 600; D: first category 680, second category 1020; E: first category 720, second category 960. Average total = (total A + total E)/2. The second category is 3/5 of that average.

questions.stem: [Table set] A fee of ₹20 applies to each in the approved category and ₹15 to each in the rejected category at B. What is the total fee collected (₹)?

Fee = 1520×20 + 1140×15.

questions.stem: [Table set] The combined total at A and D is what percentage more or less than the total at C? Give the absolute percentage difference, rounded to two decimals.
questions.explanation: Answer: 141.43. Derived data: A: first category 960, second category 720; B: first category 1520, second category 1140; C: first category 800, second category 600; D: first category 680, second category 1020; E: first category 720, second category 960. Percentage difference = |total(A)+total(D)−total(C)| ÷ total(C) × 100.

questions.explanation: Answer: 16.67. New quantity / old quantity = 100/120. Reduction percentage = 20/120 ×100.

questions.stem: Two articles are sold for ₹2200 each. One earns 20% profit and the other incurs 25% loss. Find the combined cost price (₹, to two decimals).
questions.explanation: Answer: 4766.67. Recover each cost separately: 2200×100/120 + 2200×100/75. Equal selling prices do not imply equal costs.

questions.stem: A sum of ₹12000 earns ₹7200 simple interest in 3 years. At the same annual rate, what would be the amount (₹) after 2 years with annual compounding?
questions.explanation: Answer: 17280. Rate = interest ×100/(principal ×3) = 20%. Compound amount = 12000 × (1 + 20/100)².
